title: SCH-CNT-002 weapon branch definition
description: A weapon branch definition. The project-owned typed validator in src/MechaMiner.Content/Categories/ remains authoritative; this schema is the draft 2020-12 mirror kept for editor and tool interoperability, and a fixture corpus proves the two reach the same accept/reject verdict on every structural case. See content/schemas/README.md.

id.title: A stable, case-sensitive ASCII content ID

weapon_id.description: The one weapon this branch registers against, which is the weapon this branch's own ID names. Exactly-one is structural here rather than a count: the field is a scalar, so an array of two is a type error.

branch_class.description: Which of the three transformation classes this branch is. The field is branch_class and never class: it says what the value classifies, and class is a keyword a typed model would have to escape.

cost_material_id.description: The resource this branch is fabricated from.

cost_units.description: How many units it costs. A field rather than a constant: every accepted branch costs two, and the agreement is worth asserting from the data rather than assuming from the schema.

minimum.derivation: the section makes integer currency and rank values integral in source; a count of things that exist begins at one, because a count of zero is the absence of the field rather than a value of it

behavior_kind.description: The registered behavior modifier. A lower-kebab-case token. Whether it resolves to exactly one registered behavior descriptor is the behavior registry's check and is deliberately not asserted here.

effects.title: A registry-owned parameter map
effects.description: The modifier's parameters, keyed by its behavior kind. The key vocabulary belongs to the registered behavior descriptor rather than to this schema, so keys are not enumerated here; the strict codec still rejects a null, a duplicate key, and a non-snake_case key inside one.

exclusivity.title: A branch's exclusivity
exclusivity.description: What committing to this branch rules out.

irreversible_within_run.description: Whether committing to this branch lasts the run. The longer name is the accurate one: the rule it replaced scopes irreversibility to the run, and a branch is not irreversible across runs.

mutually_exclusive_with.description: The sibling branches installing this one rules out: exactly the other two of the same weapon.

minItems.derivation: a weapon has three branches and installing one commits to it for the run, so each branch rules out the other two; the floor is three minus one and moves with the branch count

maxItems.derivation: the same three minus one as the floor, and for the same reason: a branch that ruled out a third sibling would be naming a branch of some other weapon

global_attack_rate_mapping.title: The global attack rate mapping
global_attack_rate_mapping.description: Arrays of timing names rather than one sentence each, so a future validator can check that every listed timing is a timing the weapon has. The timing vocabulary is not closed: no accepted document enumerates one, and closing it from fifteen authored sentences would be inventing it.

affected_timings.description: The timings the global Attack Rate statistic reaches.

expected_effect.title: A branch's expected effect
expected_effect.description: One field, not the two field names that carried the same concept. qualitative is required and magnitude is omitted where unquantified, which is the shape that makes 'unquantified' expressible without a second field name.

qualitative.description: The scene in which this branch is favourable.

magnitude.title: A registry-owned parameter map
magnitude.description: The approximate magnitude, omitted where the effect is unquantified. The key vocabulary belongs to the registered behavior descriptor rather than to this schema, so keys are not enumerated here; the strict codec still rejects a null, a duplicate key, and a non-snake_case key inside one.

rules.description: The accepted rule sentences for this branch.

version.title: A positive integer version
version.description: The initial schema_version and content_version of every first-authored definition is 1.

minimum.derivation: the initial value of every first-authored definition is 1 and both versions only ever increment, so no valid version is below 1; there is no upper bound because a definition may be revised without limit

name_key.title: Localization key for the player-facing name

summary_key.title: Localization key for the concise player-facing summary

tags.title: Closed query and tooling vocabulary
tags.description: The vocabulary starts empty, so [] is the only accepted value.

presentation_id.title: Logical presentation entry, required absent
presentation_id.description: Required absent: a definition carrying this field is an error. No accepted document says what a presentation definition contains, so no ID grammar has been minted for one, and minting a shape for a category with zero members would be inventing structure ahead of need. The field was declared-optional with a non-empty-string constraint, which accepted any string an author invented and validated nothing about it; rejecting the field outright fails loudly the first time somebody adds one instead of accepting an unauthorized value. The subschema is 'not' over the empty schema, which rejects every instance, so the fault is the field's presence rather than its shape and an authored empty string is rejected by the same rule rather than as an empty declared-optional field. The typed validator reports MMC-2010 and names the field. When an accepted document mints a presentation ID grammar, this declaration becomes that grammar; until then it has no minLength, because a length bound on a value that can never be authored explains nothing.
